references.text: Rebekah dresses Jacob in Esau's best clothes and covers his hands and neck with goat skins, which explains why Isaac recognizes the smell of Esau's clothes in verse 27.
Esau is described as hairy at birth, which explains why Rebekah used goat skins to imitate him—and why Isaac had to use his sense of smell to identify his son.
The content of the blessing Isaac pronounces after smelling the clothes: dew from heaven, fertility of the earth, and dominion over nations.
The scent of the clothes is compared to the fragrance of Lebanon—a thematic parallel to Isaac's words that his son's scent is like the scent of a field the Lord has blessed.
The book of Hebrews mentions Isaac's blessing of Jacob and Esau as an example of faith, highlighting the spiritual significance of the blessing in Genesis 27:27.
Isaac blesses Jacob again before sending him to Paddan-Aram, confirming Abraham's blessing over him—a reaffirmation of the blessing given in verses 27:27–29.
The contrast between Isaac's blessing of the deceptive son based on the scent of his clothes and the Father's confirmation of the true Son's identity.
The contrast between Isaac's mistaken blessing of Jacob and the Father's correct affirmation of Jesus as the beloved Son.
The contrast between Isaac's blessing based on the scent of the clothes and the Father's confirmation of the true Son.
The contrast between Isaac's blessing of the deceptive son and the Father's authoritative confirmation of Jesus.
